summary: Repaired an internal contradiction in the replay-completion account that my previous successor introduced: the older limitation entry still said the boundary case used one batch size after the extended harness had measured it at two, while the newly appended entry said the opposite. The two are merged into the single entry now reading that the boundary spans two batch sizes (16 and the default 64) with one run per side at the larger one, and the account's limitations are back to four statements - harness scope, parameter coverage, schedule variation and the caller-side dependency of the bound's input - with a consistency note in the rationale explaining the merge. Sources, executions, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are unchanged, and this repairs the last known inconsistency in the run's records: both investigations stand with their defect judgments, verified citations, answered gaps and reproducibility coverage, and the remaining allocation is left unused rather than spent on a probe that could not be cited before expiry.
